mainTopic: A בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב: the מחלוקת in the משנה, what case it describes, and a ברייתא on examining מומין on יום טוב
overview: The משנה finishes רבי יהודה's view: if the בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב has a מום, he may lift it out and slaughter it, and if not, he may not slaughter it. רבי שמעון says that an animal whose מום was not known before יום טוב is not מוכן. The גמרא suggests their argument is about examining מומין on יום טוב, and asks why the משנה did not teach that in a general case. It answers that the pit case teaches that we do not use a trick to lift the animal out because of צער בעלי חיים. The גמרא then asks why the משנה only says 'he may not slaughter.' The answer is that it is talking about someone who already lifted the animal out. After two more challenges, the גמרא settles on this case: the בכור had a temporary מום before יום טוב that became permanent on יום טוב, and it is still מוקצה. Finally, a ברייתא brings רבי יהודה הנשיא's ruling that an expert may go down and examine the animal. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא objects that one may not examine מומין on יום טוב, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: With a blemish, lift it and slaughter it
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יהודה's ruling in the משנה: a בכור in a pit with a מום may be lifted out and slaughtered. Without one, it may not be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it has a blemish, he may lift it out and slaughter it. If not, he may not slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of the משנה about a בכור that fell into a pit on יום טוב. This line finishes רבי יהודה's opinion: an expert checks it, and the result depends on whether there is a מום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור may only be eaten as ordinary meat if it has a disqualifying מום. So if the expert finds a מום, the animal can be raised and slaughtered for יום טוב. If there is no מום, it may not be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish. On a בכור, a lasting one allows it to be slaughtered and eaten outside the מקדש.
He may lift it up out of the pit.
He may slaughter it.

phrases.english: If it has a blemish —
he may lift it out and slaughter it,
and if not —
he may not slaughter it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a בכור found to have a מום on יום טוב may be raised and slaughtered. Otherwise it may not be slaughtered.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: A blemish not known before the holiday makes it not prepared
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון rules that a בכור whose מום was not known before יום טוב is not considered מוכן, so it may not be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: any animal whose blemish was not recognizable while it was still day, before יום טוב, is not considered prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי יהודה. Even if a מום is found now, the animal may not be slaughtered on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food used on יום טוב must be מוכן, meaning ready in a person's mind before the holiday starts. Since nobody knew before יום טוב that this בכור was permitted, it was not ready for use, so finding a מום now does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Prepared, meaning set aside in one's mind before יום טוב for use on it.
Recognizable or known.
While it was still day, before יום טוב began.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה lets the expert check and permit the בכור on יום טוב. רבי שמעון says it is forbidden because it was not מוכן before the holiday.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
any animal whose blemish is not recognizable
while it is still day,
phrases.notes: He means the day before יום טוב, before the holiday started.

phrases.english: is not among the prepared things —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור whose מום was not known before יום טוב is not מוכן and may not be slaughtered on it.

steps.title: What is the argument about? Maybe checking blemishes on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the root of the מחלוקת is. It suggests the argument is whether one may examine מומין on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What do they disagree about? If we say they disagree about examining blemishes, that רבי יהודה holds one may examine blemishes on יום טוב, and רבי שמעון holds one may not examine blemishes on יום טוב...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to find the principle behind the מחלוקת. It offers a first suggestion, and this sets up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking whether a בכור has a מום is a kind of legal ruling that permits the animal. The suggestion is that רבי יהודה allows this on יום טוב and רבי שמעון forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה.
What are they arguing about?
If we say. It introduces a suggestion that will be tested.
Examining blemishes to rule whether a בכור is permitted.
A holiday.

phrases.english: Gemara: About what do they disagree?
If we say they disagree about examining blemishes,
that Rabbi Yehuda holds:
one may examine blemishes on a Festival,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:
one may not examine blemishes on a Festival,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's analysis of the מחלוקת in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What principle underlies the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון?

steps.title: Then why not argue about checking blemishes in general?
steps.stepSummary: If the argument is only about examining מומין on יום טוב, the משנה should have taught it as a general case, not specifically a בכור in a pit.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...then let them disagree about examining blemishes in general!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from the step before. Why did the משנה choose the special case of a pit?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only issue is checking מומין, the pit adds nothing. A simple case of any בכור checked on יום טוב would teach the same idea. The detail of the pit seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let them disagree, meaning they should have argued about a different case.
In general, of ordinary cases.

phrases.english: then let them disagree about examining blemishes in general!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion offered in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of the case of a בכור in a pit in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the argument is only about examining מומין, the pit detail is extra. A general case would have been enough.

steps.title: The pit case teaches: no trick to rescue it
steps.stepSummary: The pit case was needed. Otherwise we might think that because of צער בעלי חיים one may use a trick to lift the animal out, like רבי יהושע. The משנה teaches that we may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of a בכור that fell into a pit was needed. You might have thought that because of the animal's suffering, one should use a trick and lift it out, following רבי יהושע. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what the pit case adds. It adds that the argument holds even when the animal is suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal stuck in a pit is suffering, and רבי יהושע elsewhere allows a clever workaround to rescue such an animal. The משנה picked the pit case to show that, even so, we do not use a trick here. The rule follows the מחלוקת about the מום.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, which is holy.
The suffering of living creatures, which the Torah cares about.
To use a trick or workaround to get around a prohibition.
You might have thought. It introduces a mistaken idea.
It teaches us, meaning the משנה is telling us something new.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the משנה ignores the animal's suffering completely. The point is only that we don't use a trick to lift it out just in order to slaughter it.

phrases.english: A firstborn that fell into a pit was necessary for him,
it would enter your mind to say:
because of the suffering of living creatures
one should use a trick and lift it out
like Rabbi Yehoshua —
phrases.notes: רבי יהושע allows a workaround elsewhere (דף ל״ז) to rescue an animal from a pit on יום טוב.

phrases.english: it teaches us.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the extra detail in the case. The pit adds a new lesson.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of צער בעלי חיים, one may use a trick to lift the בכור out, as רבי יהושע allows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that no such trick is used. The outcome depends only on the מחלוקת about the מום.

steps.title: Then it should say 'not lift and slaughter'
steps.stepSummary: If the lesson is about not lifting the animal out, the משנה should have said 'he may not lift it and slaughter it,' not just 'he may not slaughter it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say 'he may not slaughter'? It should have said 'he may not lift it out and slaughter it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from the step before by looking at the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer said the משנה teaches that we may not lift the animal out with a trick. But the משנה's negative wording only forbids slaughtering. It does not mention lifting, so the wording doesn't fit the answer.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. It shows that a challenge follows from what was just said.
It should have said.

phrases.english: If so,
"he may not slaughter"?
It should have said "he may not lift it out and slaughter"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 5 based on the משנה's wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the pit case teaches not to lift the animal with a trick.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's words 'לא ישחוט' only forbid slaughtering, not lifting. So the משנה doesn't seem to be talking about lifting.

steps.title: He already lifted it out wrongly; still no slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about someone who broke the rule and already lifted the animal out. We might think he may now slaughter it, so the משנה teaches that he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he went ahead and lifted it out. You might think he may now slaughter it, so the משנה teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording challenge. The משנה is describing what happens after someone already lifted the animal out against the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the animal is out of the pit, a person might think that since the lifting is done, slaughtering is fine. The משנה says 'לא ישחוט' to teach that even then it may not be slaughtered. This explains why the wording mentions only slaughtering.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed for this specific case.
He transgressed, meaning he did what he shouldn't have.
He may slaughter it.

steps.whatToRemember: The pit case teaches that we do not use a trick to raise the בכור. 'לא ישחוט' covers someone who already lifted it out: he still may not slaughter it.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary —
where he transgressed and lifted it out,
it would enter your mind to say:
he may slaughter it,
it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case. The משנה is about someone who already lifted the animal out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once he has already lifted it out, he may go ahead and slaughter it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even after lifting it out against the rule, he may not slaughter it.

steps.title: How could anyone think an unblemished בכור may be slaughtered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 7. A בכור with no מום may never be slaughtered, so there was nothing for the משנה to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: He may slaughter it?! But it is unblemished!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. It asks why the משנה would need to say 'don't slaughter it' when the animal is a perfect בכור, which is forbidden to slaughter anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the גמרא said the משנה teaches that even after the animal was lifted out, it may not be slaughtered. But a בכור without a מום can never be slaughtered outside the בית המקדש. So nobody would have thought it was allowed, and that answer seems useless.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal. It is holy and may only be slaughtered for eating if it has a מום.
Unblemished, whole; an animal with no מום.

phrases.english: He may slaughter it?!
But it is unblemished!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the משנה forbids slaughtering after the animal was already lifted out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unblemished בכור can never be slaughtered, so there would be no reason to think it is allowed.

steps.title: The animal got a blemish after it fell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is where the בכור got a מום, so we might have thought slaughtering it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where a blemish developed in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It says the animal got a מום, perhaps from the fall, so it is no longer תם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once there is a מום, a בכור can normally be slaughtered and eaten. So now it makes sense that someone might think it is allowed. The משנה would then be teaching that he still may not slaughter it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for (a specific case); this introduces a narrower case.
A blemish or defect that allows a בכור to be slaughtered.

phrases.english: It is needed only
where a blemish developed in it.
phrases.notes: He means the blemish came after it fell into the pit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by changing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the בכור developed a מום after it fell, one might think that once it has been lifted out he may slaughter it.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה's 'לא ישחוט' teaches that even though it now has a מום, he may not slaughter it. Step 10 then challenges this answer.

steps.title: But the animal is מוקצה!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new answer. If the מום only came on יום טוב, the animal was not fit to eat when יום טוב began, so it is מוקצה. Obviously it may not be slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of Step 9. It says the animal is clearly forbidden as מוקצה, so again nobody would think it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב started, the בכור had no מום and could not be eaten. So nobody had it in mind as food, which makes it מוקצה for the whole יום טוב. Since this is obvious, the משנה would not need to teach it.

keyTerms.meaning: Something set aside from use, because it was not ready for use when שבת or יום טוב began.
The day before יום טוב.

phrases.english: But it is muktze!
phrases.notes: When יום טוב began it had no blemish, so nobody planned to eat it.

steps.kashyaTarget: The case where the מום developed after the fall.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The animal was not fit to eat at the start of יום טוב, so it is clearly מוקצה and obviously forbidden. That leaves no חידוש.

steps.title: A temporary blemish before יום טוב that became permanent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new case. Before יום טוב the animal had a temporary מום, and on יום טוב it became permanent. We might think the owner already had the animal in mind as food, so it is not מוקצה. The משנה teaches it is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: the case is where a temporary blemish developed in it before יום טוב, and now it has become a permanent blemish. You might have said that his mind was on it, so he may slaughter it. The משנה teaches us that he may not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its last answer and gives a better case, where we really could have thought slaughtering is allowed. It then explains that the משנה teaches us that it is still not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A temporary מום does not allow a בכור to be slaughtered. But since there was already some מום before יום טוב, we might think the owner was hoping to eat it, so it is not מוקצה. The משנה teaches that this is not enough: it was not fit before יום טוב, so it stays מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary blemish that may heal. It does not allow a בכור to be slaughtered.
A permanent blemish that does allow a בכור to be slaughtered.
You might have said; this introduces the mistaken first thought.
His mind was on it; he already had it in mind for use.
It teaches us (the new point).

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'he may not slaughter it' is about a בכור whose temporary מום from before יום טוב became permanent on יום טוב. It is still מוקצה, because it was not fit to eat when יום טוב began.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think any מום before יום טוב makes the animal ready. Only a permanent מום allows slaughtering, so a temporary one leaves the animal מוקצה.

phrases.english: Rather: where a temporary blemish developed in it
on the eve of the Festival,
and now it has become a permanent blemish.
You might have said: his mind was on it,
phrases.notes: Because of the temporary blemish, we might think he was already planning to eat it before יום טוב.

phrases.english: and so he may slaughter it,
it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: דִּנְפַל בֵּיהּ מוּם עוֹבֵר מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10 with a new case that has a real reason to think it is allowed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New case (אוקימתא) with a real הוה אמינא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A temporary מום before יום טוב means the owner had the animal in mind, so it is not מוקצה and may be slaughtered.
steps.terutzMaskana: It was still unfit before יום טוב, so it is מוקצה and may not be slaughtered.

steps.title: A ברייתא: an expert may go down and check the animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה הנשיא's view. If an unblemished בכור fell into a pit, an expert goes down and checks it. If it has a מום, it may be lifted out and slaughtered. If not, it may not be slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: about an unblemished בכור that fell into a pit, רבי יהודה הנשיא says an expert goes down and examines it. If it has a blemish, he lifts it out and slaughters it. If not, he does not slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא on the same case as the משנה. It gives רבי יהודה הנשיא's ruling, which allows checking the animal on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא, examining a מום on יום טוב is allowed. The expert can check whether the fall caused a permanent מום, and if so the animal may be slaughtered. This sets up the next step, where someone objects to examining מומין on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: An expert who can decide whether a מום is the kind that allows a בכור to be slaughtered.
A pit or cistern.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main opinion that allows examining מומין on יום טוב. It is the view the next step objects to.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
An unblemished firstborn that fell into a pit,
Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says:
An expert goes down and examines it,
if it has a blemish,
he lifts it out and slaughters it,
and if not, he does not slaughter it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּכוֹר תָּם שֶׁנָּפַל לַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא on the same case, connected to the question in Step 3 about examining מומין on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An expert may examine a בכור in a pit on יום טוב. If it has a מום, it may be lifted out and slaughtered; if not, it may not be slaughtered.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא: one may not examine blemishes on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא objects that the earlier Sages already said one may not examine מומין on יום טוב. He starts to explain, beginning with a מום that appeared before יום טוב. The text continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא said to him: They already said that one may not examine blemishes on יום טוב. How so? If a blemish came into being before יום טוב, one may not examine it on יום טוב. If a blemish came into being...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן מנסיא challenges רבי יהודה הנשיא using an earlier rule. He begins to explain that rule case by case, and his explanation continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה הנשיא let the expert examine the animal on יום טוב. רבי שמעון בן מנסיא says that goes against an accepted rule: no examining מומין on יום טוב. Even a מום from before יום טוב may not be examined on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: One does not examine blemishes (on יום טוב).
Inspect, check (a מום).
How so? This introduces an explanation with cases.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ אֵין רוֹאִין מוּמִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: They already said: one may not examine blemishes on a Festival.
How so?

phrases.aramaic: נוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: If a blemish came into being on the eve of the Festival,
one may not examine it on the Festival.
If a blemish came into being

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא: הֲרֵי אָמְרוּ אֵין רוֹאִין מוּמִין בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to רבי יהודה הנשיא's ruling in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה הנשיא's ruling that an expert may examine the animal on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is an accepted rule that one may not examine מומין on יום טוב, even for a מום that appeared before יום טוב.
